page: Amazon Web Services m8g.48xlarge is an arm64 enterprise instance built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor, utilizing the AWS Graviton ARMv9 Neoverse-V2 architecture. It features 192 dedicated physical cores operating at 2.7 GHz, providing a direct one-to-one mapping between vCPUs and physical cores without simultaneous multithreading. Memory allocation totals 768.0 GB, maintaining a balanced general-purpose ratio of 4.0 GB per core. The instance provides a baseline network bandwidth of 50 Gbps. It contains no bundled local instance storage, requiring remote storage volumes for persistence, and includes zero GPU accelerators.

Benchmark evaluations highlight substantial multi-core scaling alongside moderate single-core throughput. In synthetic tests, the instance records top-tier performance in multi-core stress-ng workloads, Clang software builds, and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression, alongside strong Geekbench multi-core ratings. Single-core evaluations, including Geekbench and single-core stress-ng, place within the median range. Memory bandwidth is prominent, reaching 895.04 GB/sec on uncached 256 MB reads and 426.41 GB/sec on large block writes. Application benchmarks demonstrate top-tier execution in database operations, static web throughput reaching 168.21 GB/sec, and Redis SET throughput exceeding 356 million operations per second.

The primary architectural tradeoff lies between per-thread execution speed and aggregate multi-core density. While single-thread-bound tasks do not gain a distinct advantage, concurrent and parallel processes benefit from 192 independent execution pipelines free of hyperthreading contention. Because there is no integrated local NVMe storage, I/O-intensive workloads rely entirely on external network-attached storage over the 50 Gbps fabric. With its dense core count and memory pool, m8g.48xlarge provides strong resource density and qualitative cost efficiency for highly parallel enterprise workloads, including large-scale CI/CD build farms, static web serving fleets, in-memory caching tiers, microservices clusters, and distributed data processing pipelines.
description: Amazon Web Services m8g.48xlarge is a general purpose instance powered by AWS Graviton generation 8 architecture. Built on the Nitro hypervisor, it provides 192 dedicated arm64 physical cores using the ARMv9 Neoverse-V2 design clocked at 2.7 GHz, paired with 768.0 GB of system memory at a consistent 4.0 GB per core ratio. The instance features a 50 Gbps baseline network interface, contains no bundled local storage, and includes no discrete GPU hardware. Benchmark results demonstrate exceptional multi-core throughput, achieving top-tier ratings in stress-ng multi-core testing, Clang software compilation, multi-threaded bzip3 decompression, and Redis SET transactions exceeding 356 million operations per second. However, single-core processing scores sit within the middle tier. From a cost-efficiency perspective, the high physical core count delivers dense compute capacity without hyperthreading overhead. The m8g.48xlarge is designed for distributed microservices, static web serving fleets, enterprise databases, CI/CD compilation pipelines, and high-concurrency memory-intensive applications.
